new_result.name: QFORM-NEAR-COLOOP-OPTIMAL-VOLUME-VS-RIDGE-v1
new_result.summary: For an explicit dense-entry rotated cross block with singular values (2,2,epsilon), weak-pair volume masses (1-eta,eta), and two flat strong banks, the globally KL-optimal admissible 3-volume weight and q are explicit. Every optimized volume certificate still costs at least const*epsilon^(-1/3), whereas adjoining one untouched original square gives a uniform ridge bound <11.084.

partner_application: account03/B04 r23 gives rho=1 and A(L,rho)>3/4 on this same near-coloop block, identifying it as outside that volume-stability exit.
source_application: e5 Theorem D gives ||p||inf <=6sqrt(e)[32 epsilon^2 sqrt(eta(1-eta))]^(-1/6) at the exact q=1 optimal admissible weight.
next_step: Prove a structural ridge-or-hub alternative for near-coloop cuts without assuming a nonzero scalar pivot or a uniformly good local minor.
